explanation: Requested kinematics (W = 1.6 GeV, Q² = 1.0 GeV², cosθ* = 0, 25 φ* points spanning 0–345°) are physically valid for eta electroproduction: W = 1.6 GeV is well above the pη threshold (≈ 1.4915 GeV) and inside the EtaMAID-2023 table range (W = 1.4856–6 GeV, Q² = 0–5 GeV² per mpintp.inc), and cosθ* = 0 is inside the physical [-1, 1] range. All 4 kinematic arrays (W, Q², cosθ*, φ*) have exactly N = 25 entries as required. φ* values are a uniform 25-point grid from 0° to 345° inclusive (step = 14.375°) exactly as specified in the request. Held-fixed W and Q² values are repeated 25 times to match array length, following the convention shown in the repo's own multi-point examples (input_single_chunk.dat, input_multi_chunk.dat). Only one input file was needed: the exclurad.F Fortran reader uses list-directed I/O (`read(5,*)(w_input(i),i=1,npoi)`), which is whitespace-delimited and continues across line breaks until npoi tokens are consumed (array dimension npoimax=10000, line 18 of exclurad.F). The README's statement that N is 'limited to 10 per file' is a convention used by the batch/Slurm runner scripts (which stage one input.dat at a time), not an actual limitation of the Fortran parser -- this is confirmed by the repo's own input_multi_chunk.dat example, which packs N = 50 points into wrapped 10-column rows in a single file for one exclurad.exe invocation. Following that same convention, the 25-point arrays here are wrapped as two full rows of 10 values plus one row of 5 values per kinematic variable, with the standard eta-channel defaults (model=3 maid2000/EtaMAID, ivec=1 recoil proton, bmom=6.53 GeV CLAS12 beam momentum, vcut=0.166 GeV² CLAS12 inelasticity cut, rc_mode=0 full O(alpha) correction) taken from eta/input.dat and eta/examples/. No physical corrections were required; the request maps directly onto a single valid input file with no multi-file chunking needed.
